The largest movement in this week's data was also the easiest to misread. The China/Eastern Border channel rose by 59.8 percentile points, yet the underlying news flow was dominated not by military escalation but by diplomacy. Coverage centred on Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri's visit to Beijing, where both sides reaffirmed the importance of maintaining peace along the Line of Actual Control, alongside repeated reports denying fresh Chinese encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh. Even cultural events such as the Tawang pilgrimage contributed to sustained media attention. The result is a useful reminder that heightened salience should not automatically be interpreted as heightened danger.

This distinction lies at the heart of the IGRM framework. Traditional risk indices often blur attention with threat, treating every surge in coverage as evidence of worsening conditions. A salience monitor asks a different question: what is dominating the information environment? This week, the answer was diplomacy. The border became more visible in public discourse precisely because negotiations, official statements and competing narratives were unfolding simultaneously. Visibility increased even as the underlying message remained one of maintaining stability.

The decline in the US & Trade Policy channel tells a similar story from the opposite direction. Despite another round of tariff headlines, uncertainty eased after greater clarity emerged around the Section 301 measures and India's effective tariff position. Once the policy path became clearer, media attention naturally subsided. As the policy-uncertainty literature has long documented, markets often react less to the size of a policy than to the uncertainty surrounding it.

One number is worth remembering: 98.6. Shipping & Chokepoints remained the highest-scoring channel for a second straight week. Unlike the headline-grabbing swings elsewhere, maritime coverage continues to represent the most persistent source of geopolitical attention affecting India. It is the quiet constant in an otherwise rapidly changing geopolitical landscape.
